name: proton
description: Proton Mail, Pass, Drive, and VPN access via the Proton Bridge desktop app. 31 tools across IMAP/SMTP mail, pass-cli credentials, rclone-backed Proton Drive, and an IP-based VPN status check.

bridge_host.title: Bridge Host
bridge_host.description: Host where Proton Bridge is running. Almost always 127.0.0.1 — Bridge listens on localhost by default. Change only if you run Bridge on a different machine on your LAN (e.g. a homelab box) and point this client at it.

imap_port.title: IMAP Port
imap_port.description: Local IMAP port exposed by Proton Bridge. Default is 1143. If you've changed it, look it up in Bridge → Settings → Advanced → Mail Connection Settings.

smtp_port.title: SMTP Port
smtp_port.description: Local SMTP port exposed by Proton Bridge. Default is 1025. Same place as IMAP port — Bridge → Settings → Advanced → Mail Connection Settings.

bridge_user.title: Proton Email
bridge_user.description: Your full Proton account email (e.g. you@proton.me, you@protonmail.com, or your custom-domain Proton address). This is the account Bridge is signed into.

bridge_pass.title: Bridge App Password
bridge_pass.description: The per-app password Bridge generated for you — NOT your Proton account password. Get it from Bridge → your account → Mailbox details → IMAP/SMTP password. It looks like a random 16-character string. Stored encrypted by Claude Desktop's secret store.

bridge_from.title: From Email
bridge_from.description: Address that appears in the From: header of mail you send. Usually the same as Proton Email, but Bridge also accepts any alias you have configured on your Proton account (e.g. alias@yourdomain.com). Replies and forwards honor this too.

signature.title: Email Signature (HTML)
signature.description: Optional. Raw HTML appended to every outgoing message — send, reply, and forward. Supports inline images via base64 data URIs, hyperlinks, and formatted text. Leave blank for no signature. If you set both an HTML signature here and send a plain-text body, the body is auto-promoted to HTML so the signature renders correctly.
